slides.title: Daily Life & Communication
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 4 English, Unit 1: Daily Life & Communication. In Unit 1 you explore daily life and communication: what people do every day, and how they share their ideas. You read about routines, letters and mail, steady effort and fairness, and you meet Amal, who interviews Omar at the town post counter. You learn verb patterns, adverbs with the present simple, have got, Wh- questions, imperatives and conjunctions, using the twenty Unit 1 words. By the end you can interview someone about their work and write a fair, clear report about them. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Talk and write about your daily routine and the things you do every day.
Explain why communication, including letters, mail and language, matters to a community.
Use verb patterns correctly, for example agrees to send and enjoys playing.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to talk and write about your daily routine and the things you do every day. You will also explain why communication, including letters, mail and language, matters to a community. You will also use verb patterns correctly, for example agrees to send and enjoys playing. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: mail, language, citizen, agree, continue, gain. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: A Day at the Post Counter
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes A Day at the Post Counter and My Daily Routine. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Verb Patterns
bullets: A verb pattern is the way we join a verb to the word that follows it. Some verbs take to and another verb, and some take a verb ending in -ing. Choosing...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Verb Patterns. A verb pattern is the way we join a verb to the word that follows it. Some verbs take to and another verb, and some take a verb ending in -ing. Choosing the right pattern keeps your sentences clear. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Describe Your Daily Routine. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
